title: QB9_A#q7 still named sewage sludge among the London Protocol's explicitly permitted substances after Resolution LP.6(17) removed it from Annex 1
authority: PRIMARY, reused from CORR-LP617-SEWAGE-SLUDGE-20261028 (no new source research for this proposition). (1) Resolution LP.6(17), adopted 7 October 2022 by the Seventeenth Meeting of Contracting Parties to the 1996 Protocol, Annex: Annex 1 paragraph 1 'Delete sub-paragraph 1.2 ... .2 sewage sludge; Renumber the subsequent sub-paragraphs'; operative: no new permits for dumping sewage sludge after entry into force; active permits may be maintained until the expiry date, but not later than 31 May 2027. Registered as SRC-IMO-LP6-17. (2) Status of IMO Treaties Vol. II, 30 September 2026: the 2022 amendments entered into force on 15 January 2023 under Article 22.4. Registered as SRC-IMO-STATUS-TREATIES-VOL2-2026-09-30.
rationale: Follow-up A of known_traps entry 141, opened by CORR-LP617-SEWAGE-SLUDGE-20261028 and scheduled by the Founder on 30 Oct 2026 as a separately governed correction. The London Convention limb of Q7 gave sewage sludge as an example of an explicitly permitted substance under the 1996 Protocol, contradicting the corrected QB1_A Q13. The example list now reads dredged material, fish waste and organic material of natural origin (the Annex 1 wording; 'organic waste' was the card's paraphrase); a following sentence states the deletion by LP.6(17), adopted 7 October 2022 and in force 15 January 2023, and the permit rule (no new permits; existing permits not beyond 31 May 2027); the reg-box gains the LP.6(17) row used on QB1_A Q13; v1.1 -> v1.2. The 15- and 60-second answers do not name sewage sludge and are unchanged.
